newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CSFB analyst still sees Swiss rate cut possible.
newsitem.headline: CSFB analyst still sees Swiss rate cut possible.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston Swiss equity analyst Bernhard Tschanz said he thought the Swiss National Bank (SNB) could loosen monetary policy even further and perhaps cut its discount rate again to help spur growth.

In a commentary for the Finanz und Wirtschaft newspaper, he said Swiss shares were poised to rise further as ample liquidity makes its way into stocks already supported by the weak Swiss franc and increased buying from foreign investors.
"This favourable development on the bourse will continue because the SNB will loosen monetary policy again on account of the growth and structural crisis," Tschanz wrote.
"The discount rate may therefore, be cut again. Capital market rates will also dip slightly," he said.
His comments reflect divisions among SNB watchers on what course the central bank will take as it seeks to help the economy out of six years of stagnation without fuelling inflationary pressure.
CSFB has said before it thinks a discount rate cut is possible, but other analysts have focused more on the chances for money market rates to ease rather than seen a change in the discount rate.
Although inactive at present, the Swiss discount rate is psychologically important and is seen as the floor for money market rates.

SNB chief economist Georg Rich said this week he saw no need to boost interest rates at this stage because the economy remained weak but added, there was also no special case for rates to go down further.
In a speech on Monday, he made clear the SNB did not want to let inflation get out of control.

The SNB last cut its discount rate by half a point in September to match a historic low of 1.0 percent. It has said it will keep monetary policy generous until it detects clear signs that the economy is turning up.
